scope: Proposition 6.5 (Mean-flow circuit) of the manuscript “Subpolynomial query complexity for well-conditioned log-concave sampling” (preprints/Subpolynomial-query-complexity-for-well-conditioned-log-concave-sampling-September-26-2026/article.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 139 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 9e9a41553023f95e), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 30. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For ideal independent anchors Y0 ∼ ξ∗ and G0 ∼ N(0, Id), and every fixed J ≥ 1, the circuit (6.16) can be chosen to differ in RMS by at most polylog(d)σδJ D from the exact path integral (5.4). The approximate joint states have RMS errors at most polylog(d)δJ D. Every integration uses O(J + 1) Picard layers, with a bound independent of w and all interpolation orders.
